summary: Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).
Yunxi Wang was a Sinologist who studied at Fudan University from circa 1947 to 1951. He later held an academic post at Fudan University from circa 1952 to 2014.
Yunyao Zhai works in Indology. A Ph.D. candidate in South Asian Studies at Harvard University (attested 2026), she also holds an academic post in South Asian Studies at Harvard.

Yuri Gankovsky was a historian and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University (~1937–1942). He taught at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1945–1954) and served as secretary at the University of Chicago (1959–1964).

Yuri Levada studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1956–1972), the Institute of Sociology (~1966–1972), the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, VTSIOM (~1988–2003), and the Levada Center (~2003–2006).

Yuri Parfionovich specialized in Tibetology and Sinology, studying under George de Roerich and Bidia Dandaron. After graduating from the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies by 1953, he worked there as a naučnyj sotrudnik in 1953.
Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1936 to 1939 and later served as a professor there from circa 1968 to 1987.

Yusho Miyasaka was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe. He held posts at Koyasan University, Nagoya University (Professor Emeritus 1977–1984), Chisan Denpōin, and Shuchiin University.

Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and held posts at Hanazono University (lecturer, attested 1987) and Ryukoku University (assistant professor attested 1987–1999; professor attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University and served at Doho University from circa 1971 to 2005, where he became Emeritus Professor.

Yutaka Hirata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyushu University and held posts at the Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1955–1965), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2002).

Yutaka Iwamoto studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University (~1930–1933) under Toru Haneda, Hidenaka Tanaka, Atsuuji Ashikaga, and Ryosaburo Sakaki. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Science, Tokai University, Kyoto Tachibana University, and Soka University.

Yutaka Kanazawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Ryukoku University in 2010 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura and co-supervisor Masaaki Noni, having also studied under Kōgi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, and Isao Shimizu.

Yutaka Kawasaki works in Indology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Seio Okuda. He has held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and under Louis Renou, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986) and Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University from circa 1970 to 1999.

Yutaka Yoshida studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi, Tokyo, and Kyoto universities. A scholar of history, Japanology, and linguistics, he held multiple academic posts at Hitotsubashi University (1983–2018; Emeritus 2018) and a professorship at Kyoto University (2006).

Yutaka Yuda was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Hajime Nakamura and completed degrees at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held assistant professorships at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Yutang Lin was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and the University of Leipzig under August Conrady. He held a post at Peking University from circa 1923 to 1926.

Yuto Kawamura specializes in Indology and linguistics. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and has held posts at the University of Oxford (attested 2019), Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).
